summary: Verified crawler vs browser meta consistency for /bg/car/42254427 and Cayenne 42354550 across bg/ro/en, and regression items (All-New strip, PO536 strip, image proxy, track share). All titles and cleaning rules pass. Descriptions match verbatim for the Kia Sportage 42254427 case in bg/ro/en. However a real inconsistency was found for prices with 5+ digits: crawler backend uses `{:.0f} €` (no thousand separator) while browser Intl.NumberFormat(bg-BG) inserts a NBSP thousand separator, so the same car's price is quoted in two different formats between the share page and the rendered page.

minor.issue: Price in og:description is formatted without a thousand separator (`f"{sale_eur:.0f} €"`) while the browser prints the same price with a NBSP thousand separator via Intl.NumberFormat. Observed for /bg/car/42354550: crawler ogd = '05/2020 · 12 500 km · 69599 € — крайна цена до България с мито, ДДС и доставка.' vs browser ogd = '05/2020 · 12\xa0500 km · 69\xa0599\xa0€ — крайна цена до България с мито, ДДС и доставка.'. Kia Sportage 42254427 (9199, 4 digits) happens to match because Intl produces no separator below 10000. Also crawler mileage uses regular space ('133 769') while browser uses NBSP ('133\xa0769').

The crawler share HTML sets og:description but does NOT emit a <meta name="description"> tag. The browser writes both. Not a facts-mismatch, but if Google fetches the share page it will only see og:description.

action_items: Align price formatting between backend share_car() and the frontend's Intl.NumberFormat output. Options: (a) change backend to format sale_eur with NBSP thousand separator (e.g. `f"{int(sale_eur):,} €".replace(',', '\u00a0')`), or (b) change frontend to strip the thousand separator for prices in the description. The owner's complaint is that the two sides describe the same car identically — currently they diverge on prices ≥ 10000 (Cayenne 69599, Tucson 13199, plus mileage NBSP vs plain space).
Optionally emit <meta name="description"> in the crawler share HTML for parity with the browser render.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py share_car line ~2047-2051: mileage uses `,` -> ` ` (plain space) while price uses no separator at all. Both diverge from Intl.NumberFormat('bg-BG') which uses NBSP. Centralise this so backend and frontend produce byte-identical strings.
server.py 4004 lines — file is very large; consider splitting share/OG generation into a dedicated module for testability.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Only the price/mileage whitespace formatting differs between crawler og:description and browser og:description. Facts (year 05/2020, mileage 12500, price 69599 on Cayenne; 03/2013, 133769, 9199 on Sportage) are correct on both sides. Cayenne badge_detail is empty in Encar's data — that is why only submodel '3.0 Coupe' appears (there is no trim to add). All 'PO536' / '(2019-)' / 'All New' / 'All-New' / '(JA)' cleanup passes.
rca_of_the_issue: Backend `share_car` composes the price as `f"{sale_eur:.0f} €"` producing e.g. `69599 €`. Frontend uses `Intl.NumberFormat('bg-BG', {style:'currency', currency:'EUR', maximumFractionDigits:0})` which yields `69 599 €`. For sale_eur < 10000 the JS formatter emits no thousand separator, so the two sides accidentally match. For >= 10000 they diverge. Similarly backend mileage uses ASCII space, browser uses NBSP.
